tables.products: One row per product in the catalog.
tables.orders: One row per order. Each order belongs to one customer and has one or more order_items.
tables.order_items: One row per product line in an order.

products.unit_price.description: Current list price in US dollars.

orders.status.description: Order state. Only completed orders count as revenue.

orders.total_amount.description: Order total in US dollars; equals the sum of quantity * unit_price over its order_items.

orders.shipped_date.description: Date the order shipped. NULL until it ships; only completed orders have one.

order_items.quantity.description: Units of the product in this order line.

order_items.unit_price.description: Price per unit when the order was placed, in US dollars.

glossary.definition: Money from completed orders only; pending and cancelled orders are excluded.
glossary.sql: SUM(orders.total_amount) for orders with status = 'completed'. For revenue by product or category use SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price) over order_items of completed orders.

glossary.definition: Share of all orders that were cancelled.
glossary.sql: AVG(CASE WHEN orders.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)

glossary.definition: An order with a shipped_date. Only completed orders ship.

notes: The data is a fixed snapshot. Interpret relative dates such as 'last month' or 'this year' relative to the latest order_date in the data, not today's date, and say so in assumptions.
All amounts are in US dollars.

examples.question: What was the revenue from Partner orders in the first quarter of 2025?
examples.sql: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND channel = 'Partner' AND order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2025-04-01'

examples.question: Show monthly revenue from Small business customers in 2024.
examples.sql: SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month, SUM(o.total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'Small business' AND o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

examples.question: Which 3 products appear in the most cancelled orders?
examples.sql: SELECT p.name AS product, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS cancelled_orders FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY cancelled_orders DESC LIMIT 3

examples.question: What share of Website orders were cancelled in 2025, as a percentage?
examples.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END), 1) AS cancelled_percent FROM orders WHERE channel = 'Website' AND order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2026-01-01'

examples.question: List Enterprise customers who have not ordered since the end of June 2025.
examples.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c WHERE c.segment = 'Enterprise' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.order_date > '2025-06-30')
